lines: Casey Morgan
+1 (555) 010-7731 | casey.morgan@example.com | example.com/portfolio/cmorgan
Date of birth: 3 Mar 1997 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Lakeshore University | B.A. in Cognitive Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2015 - May 2019
EXPERIENCE
Pinegrove Financial | Senior UX Researcher | Metro City, USA | Mar 2022 - Jun 2025
- Cut the card-dispute form's abandonment rate from 37% to 22% in a four-week A/B test by splitting it into three short steps with saved progress.
- Brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA by setting body-text contrast to at least 3:1 against every background.

- Synthesizing 60 interviews, 400 survey responses and 18 months of support tickets through affinity mapping, journey mapping and a tagged clip library, cut repeat support calls about statements by 23%.
- Presented quarterly findings to the head of product and two design teams; three of the top five recommended fixes shipped in the next release cycle.
- Trained 12 product managers to run their own unmoderated tests with a shared script template, which doubled the number of tests run each quarter.
- Led research on the mobile onboarding flow, testing three prototypes with 24 new customers; the shipped design raised completed sign-ups from 41% to 58% in the quarter after launch.
Northwind Health | UX Research Associate | Metro City, USA | Jul 2019 - Feb 2022
- Raised the patient app's Net Promoter Score from 6.1 to 8.4, calculated as the average 0-10 recommendation rating across 2,000 monthly survey responses.
- Interviewed 40 patients about appointment reminders; the findings led to a two-way text reminder that cut missed appointments from 14% to 9%.
- Writes the screener and consent templates for all patient studies, cutting study setup time from two weeks to three days.
- Tested the telehealth waiting-room screens with 16 older patients; the revised layout cut support calls about joining a video visit by 30%.
PROJECTS
Accessible Transit Map | Independent Project | Figma | Sep 2024 - Present
- Redesigned a city transit map for screen-reader and low-vision riders, and tested it with 12 participants on timed route-finding tasks.
- Cut median route-finding time from 90 to 60 seconds, a 50% improvement, by adding audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
- Raised task success by 20% across 12 participants, from 65% to 85%, with audio landmarks and high-contrast line colors.
Community Clinic Booking Redesign | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Figma | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Redesigned a free clinic's online booking flow, cutting the steps to book from 9 to 4; phone bookings fell by a quarter in the next two months.
- Recruited 10 clinic patients and ran two rounds of hallway testing, fixing the six issues that stopped first-time users from finishing a booking.
- Wrote the clinic's volunteer handbook for maintaining the booking pages, which two later volunteer teams used to add Spanish-language booking.
SKILLS
Tools: Figma, screen-reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA), Tableau
Methods: moderated and unmoderated usability testing, interveiws, surveys, A/B testing

items.says: Check that the portfolio link leads directly to relevant work.
Check that the contact details are current.
Remove the date of birth and nationality unless an application requests them.
items.because: They generally do not help a UX research application and take space from relevant evidence.

items.says: Clarify whether your role in the form change was research, design, or both.
items.because: The bullet credits you with a design decision without showing what you did as a researcher.

items.says: The 3:1 body-text contrast ratio does not meet the stated WCAG 2.1 AA standard.
items.because: Normal text generally requires 4.5:1; 3:1 applies to large text and certain other elements.

items.says: Narrow the claim that you brought the design system to WCAG 2.1 AA if you verified only contrast.
items.because: Full conformance involves other applicable criteria.

items.says: Change “Synthesizing” to a grammatically parallel past-tense opening.
items.because: The other bullets use past tense.

items.says: Explain what changed after the synthesis to connect it to the 23% reduction.
items.because: The connection between the findings and fewer repeat calls is unclear.

items.says: Identify what made the shipped fixes important if space permits.
items.because: “Top five” alone does not convey their impact.

items.says: Specify whether testing volume doubled among the PMs, their teams, or the organization.
items.because: The result needs a meaningful scope.

items.says: Distinguish the post-launch completion-rate change from a result attributable solely to the research.
An average recommendation rating is not Net Promoter Score.
items.because: Net Promoter Score uses the percentages of promoters and detractors.

items.says: Verify the metric’s scale and figures.
Clarify which patients or appointments the missed-appointment figures cover.
items.because: The figures may concern those affected by the reminder rather than all appointments.

items.says: Change “Writes” to past tense.
Check whether the shorter setup time is attributable to the templates.
Specify whether participants tested the redesign, an earlier version, or both.
items.because: That would make the following comparisons interpretable.

items.says: A drop from 90 to 60 seconds is a 33% reduction in time, not a 50% improvement.
The rise from 65% to 85% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
Remove the repeated design features or use the space to clarify the testing.
items.because: The preceding bullet already names the same features.

items.says: Clarify whether phone bookings fell because users moved online.
items.because: The decline alone does not establish that.

items.says: Specify how you determined that the six issues blocked completion.
Clarify your contribution to Spanish-language booking.
items.because: The wording could imply you implemented it yourself.

items.says: Consider whether your Tableau experience is evident enough elsewhere.
Correct the typo “interveiws.”
Make sure the listed methods are supported by the experience or projects above.
